items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is decode_transaction the inverse of encode_transaction?
items.test_procedure: 1. For each transaction type, create valid transaction object. 2. Encode transaction to bytes. 3. Decode bytes back to transaction object. 4. Verify decoded == original for all fields. 5. Test round-trip for adversarial field values.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0040. Boundary: tb-004. Non-bijective codec enables transaction manipulation.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does decode_transaction reject unknown type prefixes?
items.test_procedure: 1. Send bytes with type prefix 0x05 and verify TransactionTypeError. 2. Test all invalid prefixes (0x05-0xFF). 3. Verify no silent acceptance of unknown types. 4. Verify proper error propagation (not IndexError, etc.). 5. Check boundary between RLP legacy and typed transactions.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0041. Boundary: tb-004. Unknown type acceptance causes undefined behavior.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is decode_transaction crash-resistant to malformed input?
items.test_procedure: 1. Fuzz decode_transaction with random byte sequences. 2. Verify only TransactionTypeError or valid transaction returned. 3. Check no IndexError, OverflowError, MemoryError propagates. 4. Test truncated inputs, oversized inputs, malformed RLP. 5. Verify node stability under adversarial P2P traffic.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0042. Boundary: tb-004. Crash from P2P packet is critical DoS vulnerability.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are EIP-7702 authorizations bound to chain_id and nonce?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create EIP-7702 authorization with specific chain_id and nonce. 2. Verify signing_hash_7702 includes chain_id and authorization data. 3. Attempt replay with different chain_id - verify rejection. 4. Attempt replay with stale nonce - verify rejection. 5. Verify nonce must match current authorizer account nonce.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0043. Boundary: tb-008. Fusaka-related EIP-7702. Stale auth replay enables unauthorized code delegation.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction hash computation deterministic and unique?
items.test_procedure: 1. Compute hash for legacy transaction: keccak256(rlp.encode(tx)). 2. Compute hash for typed transaction: keccak256(type_prefix || tx_data). 3. Verify same transaction produces same hash across multiple calls. 4. Verify different transactions produce different hashes. 5. Test for hash collisions across transaction types.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0044. Boundary: tb-001. Non-deterministic or colliding hashes break tx tracking.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does close_state release all references?
items.test_procedure: 1. Call close_state after block finalization. 2. Verify _main_trie reference deleted. 3. Verify _storage_tries reference deleted. 4. Verify _snapshots reference deleted. 5. Verify created_accounts reference deleted. Check memory profile in long-running node.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0045. Boundary: tb-003. Memory leak affects long-running nodes.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does set_account_balance set (not add) the balance?
items.test_procedure: 1. Set account balance to value X. 2. Call set_account_balance with value Y. 3. Verify balance == Y (not X + Y). 4. Test with coinbase payment code paths. 5. Verify no ether inflation from incorrect set semantics.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0046. Boundary: tb-003. Add instead of set causes ether inflation.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does set_code trigger empty account destruction?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create account with only code (nonce==0, balance==0). 2. Call set_code with empty bytes. 3. Verify modify_state destroys the now-empty account. 4. Test with CREATE/CREATE2 deployment that fails. 5. Test EIP-7702 code delegation scenarios.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0047. Boundary: tb-003. Ghost accounts if destruction not triggered.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-155 signing hash correctly formed?
items.test_procedure: 1. Compute signing_hash_155 for test transaction. 2. Verify hash == keccak256(rlp.encode([...fields, chain_id, 0, 0])). 3. Verify trailing zeros are included. 4. Attempt cross-chain replay of EIP-155 transaction. 5. Verify different chains produce different signing hashes.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0048. Boundary: tb-009. Broken EIP-155 enables cross-chain replay attacks.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ECDSA non-repudiation property maintained?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify signing hash includes all transaction fields. 2. Verify no field can be modified without invalidating signature. 3. Verify transaction hash provides unique permanent identifier. 4. Review for any signing hash construction flaws. 5. This is primarily a cryptographic property verification.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0049. Boundary: tb-001. Non-repudiation violations require ECDSA breaks (theoretical).

items.title: Verify Conditional Scope: Are Fusaka gas economics consensus-safe under transaction ordering?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT bounds single transaction gas. 2. Verify calldata_floor is enforced regardless of ordering. 3. Test block building with various transaction orderings. 4. Compare results across client implementations. 5. Document MEV implications but note out-of-scope.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0050. CONDITIONAL SCOPE - MEV generally out-of-scope unless causing consensus failure.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does Engine API enforce full transaction validation?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify JWT authentication on Engine API endpoints. 2. Submit invalid block payload via Engine API. 3. Verify full EL transaction validation occurs. 4. Verify invalid transactions are rejected despite CL trust. 5. Test that compromised CL cannot bypass EL validation.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0051. Boundary: tb-006. CL-EL boundary. Invalid block processing causes consensus failure.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Does get_beacon_proposer_index correctly use pre-computed proposer_lookahead instead of on-demand computation?

reachability.notes: If this function falls back to on-demand computation instead of using the lookahead, it would produce different results (since state may have changed since lookahead computation), causing consensus failures.

items.test_procedure: 1. Locate the get_beacon_proposer_index function implementation. 2. Verify it accesses state.proposer_lookahead[state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] directly. 3. Confirm there is NO fallback path to on-demand computation (compute_proposer_index or equivalent). 4. Create a test case where state changes between epoch boundary and slot execution. 5. Compare the proposer index returned by lookahead-based method vs. on-demand computation to verify they could diverge. 6. Verify all code paths through get_beacon_proposer_index use the lookahead array exclusively.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-36, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: FULU-SG005-INV-001. EIP-7917 modification requires strict use of pre-computed lookahead.

items.title: Verify Consensus Layer correctly populates proposer_lookahead at epoch boundaries

Confirm the lookahead array has exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries. 4. Verify the computation uses the correct state snapshot (epoch boundary state). 5. Check that proposer_lookahead is immutable within an epoch.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-36, Supporting node: actor-consensus-layer

Test edge cases at epoch boundaries where lookahead transitions.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-36, Supporting node: actor-validator

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is fork upgrade irreversibility enforced across all state transitions at tb-007?

Check for race conditions or edge cases in fork scheduler that could cause fork oscillation. 6. Verify that beacon node rejects any state with inconsistent fork version history.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-3, Trust Boundary: tb-007, Invariant: fork-SG-001-INV-003. Fork oscillation attacks could cause network instability and consensus failure.

Test edge cases around epoch boundaries where fork transitions occur. 5. Verify scheduler rejects any attempt to schedule a downgrade.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-3, Supporting node: actor-fork-scheduler

Verify that checkpoint sync and snap sync correctly validate fork versions.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-3, Supporting node: actor-beacon-node

items.title: Can upgrade_to_fulu corrupt or drop BeaconState fields during Electra-to-Fulu fork transition?

reachability.notes: State preservation during fork is consensus-critical. Triggered automatically at fork epoch via P2P consensus.

items.test_procedure: 1. Enumerate all fields in electra.BeaconState and identify which fields are explicitly modified by upgrade_to_fulu (expected: fork, proposer_lookahead). 2. Create a pre-fork BeaconState with known values for all fields. 3. Execute upgrade_to_fulu and capture the post-state. 4. For each field NOT in the explicit modification list, assert post.F == pre.F. 5. Check for subtle corruption vectors: (a) deep-copy vs shallow-copy issues for nested structures, (b) default value initialization that overwrites existing data, (c) missing field assignments in new struct initialization, (d) type conversion errors during SSZ serialization/deserialization. 6. Verify field preservation under edge cases: maximum-size validators list, full historical roots, boundary epoch values.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-4, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-001, Assumption: asm-009. This is consensus-critical - any field corruption would cause chain splits or fund loss.

items.title: Falsification Test: Can the fork version history chain be broken during upgrade_to_fulu transition?

reachability.notes: Incorrect version chaining would cause P2P fork digest mismatches.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify the upgrade_to_fulu state transition function in the beacon node codebase. 2. Examine the implementation to verify that post.fork.previous_version is explicitly set to pre.fork.current_version. 3. Design test cases that exercise the upgrade transition with various pre-states, including edge cases (e.g., genesis fork, consecutive upgrades). 4. Verify the post-condition holds: assert(post.fork.previous_version == pre.fork.current_version). 5. Attempt to falsify by: (a) checking for any code path that could skip the version assignment, (b) testing with corrupted pre-state fork data, (c) verifying no race conditions exist in concurrent state transitions. 6. Validate that fork digest computation downstream correctly uses the maintained version chain.
items.falsification_strategy: Attempt to trigger upgrade_to_fulu with edge-case pre-states (empty version, mismatched versions, repeated upgrades) and verify whether the version chain invariant can be violated. Check for off-by-one errors in version array indexing.
items.impact_if_violated: Fork digest mismatch causing P2P network partition - nodes with broken version chains would compute different fork digests and fail to communicate with correct nodes.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-5, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-002, Assumption: asm-009. Bug bounty eligible with PoC showing fork version chain breakage.

items.title: Does upgrade_to_fulu correctly set post.fork.current_version to FULU_FORK_VERSION?

reachability.notes: Wrong fork version causes complete P2P network isolation.

items.test_procedure: 1. Locate the upgrade_to_fulu function in the state transition code. 2. Trace the assignment of post.fork.current_version to verify it uses FULU_FORK_VERSION constant. 3. Verify FULU_FORK_VERSION constant matches the expected fork version from the specification. 4. Create a test case that invokes upgrade_to_fulu and asserts post.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION. 5. Test edge cases: verify the upgrade path from the previous fork (Electra) correctly transitions to Fulu. 6. Attempt to falsify by checking if any code path could set an incorrect version or skip the version assignment.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-6, Post-condition from invariant fork-SG-002-INV-003. Incorrect fork version after upgrade causes the node to become incompatible with the network, effectively creating a network partition. This is a critical post-condition that must hold after every fork upgrade operation.

items.title: Falsification Test: Can the fork epoch in post-state diverge from the epoch at which upgrade_to_fulu was triggered?

reachability.notes: Incorrect fork epoch in state would affect epoch-dependent logic.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify the upgrade_to_fulu function in the state transition code. 2. Trace how post.fork.epoch is assigned during the upgrade. 3. Verify that get_current_epoch(pre) is correctly computed and assigned to post.fork.epoch. 4. Design test cases where pre-state has edge-case epoch values (epoch 0, max epoch, boundary epochs). 5. Attempt to trigger upgrade_to_fulu at different points in the epoch lifecycle to verify consistency. 6. Check for any code paths that could set fork.epoch to a different value than the current epoch. 7. Verify that no intermediate state modifications could cause epoch drift between reading pre-state and writing post-state.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-7, Post-condition for fork-SG-002-INV-004. This is an internal property requiring formal verification approach. Focus on proving the post-condition cannot be violated through any execution path of upgrade_to_fulu.

items.title: Can the proposer_lookahead field be incorrectly initialized during the Fulu fork upgrade, causing wrong proposer assignments?

reachability.notes: proposer_lookahead initialization affects proposer scheduling.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify the upgrade_to_fulu function in the beacon chain state transition code. 2. Verify that initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre) is called with the correct pre-state. 3. Compare post.proposer_lookahead against the expected output of initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre). 4. Test edge cases: empty validator set, maximum validator count, validators at boundary indices. 5. Verify no stale data from pre-state leaks into the new proposer_lookahead. 6. Check that proposer scheduling after the fork uses the correctly initialized lookahead. 7. Simulate a fork transition and verify proposer assignments match expectations.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-8, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-005, Assumption: asm-017. Post-condition verification for EIP-7917 proposer lookahead initialization during Fulu fork. Incorrect initialization could enable unauthorized block proposals by assigning wrong proposers.

items.title: Is the upgrade_to_fulu function pure and free of pre-state side effects?

reachability.notes: Pre-state mutation would cause non-deterministic behavior but is hard to exploit externally.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify the upgrade_to_fulu function implementation. 2. Create a deep copy of the pre-state before calling upgrade_to_fulu. 3. Execute upgrade_to_fulu with the pre-state. 4. Compare the original pre-state copy with the pre-state after execution - they MUST be identical. 5. Check for any in-place mutations of state fields, particularly mutable data structures. 6. Verify that the function returns a new state object rather than modifying the input. 7. Test with edge cases: empty states, maximum-size states, and states at fork boundaries.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-9, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-006. CONDITIONAL SCOPE: Requires further investigation to determine full bug bounty eligibility. Pre-state mutation during fork would cause non-deterministic state transitions, potentially causing consensus splits.

items.title: Falsify Fork Version Branch Exclusivity: Can compute_fork_version return ambiguous or missing results for any epoch value?

reachability.notes: Used in fork digest computation for P2P topic subscription.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify all branch conditions in compute_fork_version that determine which fork version is returned based on epoch. 2. Extract the epoch thresholds for each fork (e.g., GENESIS_EPOCH, ALTAIR_FORK_EPOCH, BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH, CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH, DENEB_FORK_EPOCH, ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH). 3. Test boundary epoch values: exactly at each fork epoch threshold, one below, one above. 4. Verify branch conditions are mutually exclusive: check that no epoch value satisfies multiple branch conditions simultaneously. 5. Verify branch conditions are exhaustive: check that every valid epoch value (0 to MAX_UINT64) satisfies exactly one branch condition. 6. Look for off-by-one errors in comparison operators (< vs <=, > vs >=). 7. Test with epoch = 0 (genesis) to ensure it returns GENESIS_FORK_VERSION. 8. Test with epoch = MAX_UINT64 to ensure the latest fork version is returned. 9. Verify the ordering of if-else branches matches the chronological order of forks to prevent earlier branches from shadowing later ones.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-11, Invariant: p2p-SG-001-INV-002. Violation would cause P2P network fragmentation where nodes on different fork versions cannot communicate, effectively partitioning the network.

items.title: Does compute_fork_version always return a valid 4-byte Version for all epochs >= 0?

reachability.notes: A null fork version would crash P2P message handling.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify the compute_fork_version function implementation. 2. Review all code paths to verify they return a valid 4-byte Version. 3. Test with edge-case epoch values: epoch=0, epoch=MAX_UINT64, epoch at fork transition boundaries. 4. Verify no code path returns null, undefined, or error for valid epoch inputs. 5. Check that fork configuration covers all possible epoch ranges without gaps. 6. Attempt to trigger function failure by providing epochs that fall between defined fork boundaries.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-12, Invariant: p2p-SG-001-INV-003. This is an internal invariant - a null or invalid return would crash the node during P2P handshake or gossip validation. Falsification approach: find edge-case epoch values that cause function to return error/null/undefined.

items.title: Can the slot modulo index into proposer_lookahead exceed valid bounds or map to an incorrect epoch proposer?

reachability.notes: An off-by-one in the modulo operation could cause an out-of-bounds access or map to the wrong slot's proposer.

items.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code locations where `slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` is computed as an index into `state.proposer_lookahead`. 2. Verify the modulo operation uses the correct divisor (SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, not SLOTS_PER_EPOCH + 1 or similar). 3. Test boundary conditions: slot values at epoch boundaries (slot 0, slot SLOTS_PER_EPOCH-1, slot SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, slot 2*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH-1). 4. Verify the computed index is always in range [0, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH) by checking array access bounds. 5. Confirm no off-by-one errors exist in the index calculation that could cause out-of-bounds access. 6. Trace the proposer assignment lookup to ensure the index correctly corresponds to the current epoch's proposer schedule.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-37, Invariant: FULU-SG005-INV-002. Pre-condition verification: The modulo operation must guarantee index bounds. An off-by-one could cause array out-of-bounds crash (DoS) or assign the wrong proposer to a slot causing missed blocks or conflicting proposals.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is sidecar.index validated to be within [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS) before processing?

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft a sidecar with an out-of-range index and send it via P2P gossip.

Craft a malicious DataColumnSidecar with index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS and send via P2P gossip. 4. Craft a malicious DataColumnSidecar with index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS + 1 and send via P2P gossip. 5. Craft a malicious DataColumnSidecar with index = MAX_UINT64 and send via P2P gossip. 6. Verify that all out-of-range sidecar messages are rejected at the gossip validation layer. 7. Confirm no array out-of-bounds access, node crash, or data corruption occurs.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-13, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Invariant: p2p-SG-002-INV-001. Boundary property with attacker-controlled input - elevated to Critical severity.

items.title: Verify Gossip Network Actor: Does the gossip network properly propagate rejection of invalid column indices?

Verify that rejection happens early in the validation pipeline to minimize resource consumption.

Test with fuzzing to ensure no edge cases allow out-of-bounds access. 6. Verify that a crash or panic cannot be triggered by malformed input.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-13, Supporting node check for actor-beacon-node. Array out-of-bounds can lead to crash, data corruption, or potentially code execution.

Review all code paths that consume kzg_commitments to ensure they handle empty arrays defensively.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does verify_data_column_sidecar reject sidecars with excessive KZG commitments beyond epoch-specific max_blobs_per_block limit?

Test boundary conditions: submit sidecar with exactly max_blobs_per_block commitments (should accept), then max_blobs_per_block + 1 (must reject). 5. Test epoch boundary scenarios: craft sidecars at slots where blob parameters change between epochs. 6. Verify rejection response does not leak internal state or cause resource exhaustion before rejection.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-15, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Invariant: p2p-SG-002-INV-003. CRITICAL: Epoch boundaries where blob parameters change are especially high-risk attack surfaces. Bug bounty eligible per source property.

items.title: Verify Gossip Network Node (actor-gossip-network): Is the P2P gossip layer properly validating sidecar commitment counts before forwarding?

items.title: Verify Beacon Node (actor-beacon-node): Does the beacon node correctly derive epoch from sidecar slot and apply the correct blob parameters?

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does verify_data_column_sidecar reject sidecars with mismatched array lengths (column, kzg_commitments, kzg_proofs)?

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft sidecar with mismatched array lengths.

Verify that length equality checks occur BEFORE any array indexing operations. 4. Craft test sidecars with: (a) len(column) > len(kzg_commitments), (b) len(column) < len(kzg_proofs), (c) len(kzg_commitments) != len(kzg_proofs). 5. Submit each malformed sidecar via P2P gossip and verify immediate rejection with appropriate error. 6. Confirm no out-of-bounds memory access occurs (use sanitizers/fuzzing). 7. Check that rejection happens at gossip layer, not deeper in processing.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W2B3-16, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Invariant: p2p-SG-002-INV-004. Mismatched lengths could cause out-of-bounds access during KZG proof verification, crashing the node.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-008: Are cell indices correctly constructed to match column index in KZG proof verification?
